method: Fresh visual inspection of contact-all35.jpg and 29 full-size images, including all revised 12 and held 059. No other review JSON read. Families use camera, figure arrangement, dominant foreground/object and action together; event titles do not define families.

groups.rationale: Two close figures bend or look downward toward large pale papers spread across a foreground horizontal surface. Chest versus desk and crouching versus standing vary, but the paper-led inspection hierarchy repeats.
Eye-level pair beside a large bare plank stall, open ledger held upright and open-hand explanation. The bare trading surface supplies the visual absence.

groups.family: Left foreground pair against rightward receding activity
groups.rationale: Document-bearing pair occupies left foreground while water/road and small moving figures or vehicle recede across the right. Setting changes do not erase this shared spatial template.

Eye-level medium/full group arranged laterally around an authoritative figure and a conspicuous extended arm/object. Adjacent observers frame the transaction. Key, shielding hand and purse differ, but this is the closest remaining repeated dramatic staging.

groups.family: Close opposed pair with hand-led demonstration
groups.rationale: Large facing figures flank a central hand action just above a low foreground support. Object handling drives the scene; background figures and setting are subordinate. Key offer and wet cloth demonstration remain distinct subject matter within this shared close interaction.

groups.family: Petitioner at a restrictive door opening
groups.rationale: Large near-left petitioner faces a right-side gatekeeper bounded by a wooden opening. Raised hand/paper and the physical door barrier dominate. Half-door versus hatch is a variation of the same staging.

groups.family: Two infrastructural poles and central comparison
groups.rationale: Well fills left edge, grain and notices fill right; the people and two purses bridge these competing assets. This object-led bilateral layout is stronger than a generic standing conversation.

groups.family: Back-view observers on a deep winter route
groups.rationale: Near-left back-view pair watches a procession shrinking toward the distant chapel. Route and depth, rather than face-to-face dialogue, govern the frame.
Fence isolates the left woman from central horse handler and right man; chest anchors bottom center. The barrier and triangular staging differ from frontal group bargaining.

groups.family: Uncovering a load toward the viewer
groups.rationale: Cart and bright timber dominate front center; large near-left worker lifts a wet cover while observers look inward. Physical reveal action supplies the focal structure.
Ox and cart span the foreground in side profile, people strung along a leftward movement. Transportation dominates the silhouette.

groups.family: Low interior chest toward distant doorway exchange
groups.rationale: Very large low-left locked chest, long floor perspective and small backlit pair at the right doorway. Strong scale/depth contrast separates it from chest inspection or frontal bargaining.
Steep overhead camera and empty rectangular chest enclosed by three crouching heads/hands; dark void and scattered tallies dominate.

Full-body central reader and pointing villager sit between a left crowd and strong right cart diagonal. Multiple depth layers and destination gesture differ from the tighter authority negotiation family.

groups.family: Single waiting figure against empty workshop
groups.rationale: One small standing figure at left, vacant bench and dark opening at right. Architectural vacancy is the main subject.
Large horse occupies left half with packed tack foreground; two upright people and bundled rolls at right. Horse scale and preparation govern the image.
Huge central back-view cloak obscures near field, small candidates and grain lie beyond. Viewer shares the evaluator's position, unlike frontal multi-person negotiation.

groups.family: Opposing pairs across a central ground marker
groups.rationale: Low central boundary stone and diverging ground surfaces separate two distant left/right pairs. Open ground and spatial division dominate.
Single large indoor custodian lifts a vertical document from left foreground chest; small paired witnesses are framed far behind at right.
Two workers at different depths handle a long diagonal beam, with one low crouching foreground body. Material and physical labor dominate.
Stone steps produce a strong descending diagonal from upper-left elder to central rider and lower-right attendant; horse and luggage carry the scene.

groups.family: Timber stack against visibly empty yard
groups.rationale: Large stacked beam ends at lower-left, two figures above them, long document vertical and pointing arm toward open right yard. This is a stock-versus-vacancy split rather than tabletop consultation.

groups.family: Paired craft stations across foreground machinery
groups.rationale: Loom on left and layered cloth on right form two large tactile foreground stations. Two workers demonstrate processes across these surfaces; no document supplies the focal point.

Five people lean inward around grain, bucket and jug; near-left and near-right bodies enclose the table. Paper is present, but collective provisions discussion and encirclement differ from two-person paper inspection.
Wattle weir and stakes run strongly from near right to distant left, with three separated workers measuring/handling the structure in water.

Two centered standing readers jointly hold a single bright square sheet at chest height, with colorful wares below and active market behind. This repeats document symbolism but differs from horizontal indoor paper inspection.

Held image: seated blue official and ledger occupy left foreground; three standing men across open right space address him. Asymmetric seated-versus-standing hearing differs from the frontal bargaining group.

pass_definition: No visual composition family exceeds 3 when camera, arrangement, foreground hierarchy and action are considered jointly. This does not claim absence of broader stylistic or motif repetition.

revised12.indoor_note: 020 is a doorway scene viewed from inside and is conservatively counted indoors; 025 is an indoor overhead chest scene. 034 is exterior-facing a half-door, not an indoor room scene.
revised12.document_note: 025 contains wooden tallies, not a dominant paper document. Revised scenes focus on keys, bags, animals, boundaries, work or relationships.

issues.note: Closest remaining repeated dramatic staging; all three use lateral group negotiation and an emphatic arm gesture. Already at the 3-image limit; avoid adding this staging.
Indoor paired paper inspection also reaches the 3-image limit. Different containers do not make these fully distinct compositions.

Standing multi-person exchanges remain common. 004 has a bilateral resource layout, 011 a fence-divided triangle and 027 a crowd/cart depth arrangement; these are not automatically the same composition, but their human-dialogue motif can still feel repetitive in sequence.
Paper/book/scroll symbolism remains frequent among retained images. Presence is not equivalent to centrality or identical staging, but the overall set has not eliminated documentary motifs.

limits: Visual family assignment is a qualitative judgment, not a mathematical uniqueness proof. A stricter art director may merge adjacent negotiation motifs and should inspect the identified boundary cluster.
All 35 were inspected on the contact sheet; 29 were additionally inspected full size. Board-only images were 008, 010, 028, 030, 035 and 042.
Review covers still-image composition and revised-scene indoor/document limits; it is not historical accuracy, anatomy, runtime integration or user acceptance approval.
059 remains held. Including it in this review does not authorize release or installation. No assets were edited.
